video.title: Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft - 9 Cat 10 Team Pick 4

summary: Josh Lloyd runs a 10-team, 9-category mock draft from pick 4. After Jokic, Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander went 1 to 3, he took Luka Doncic. His next picks were Kevin Durant, Anthony Davis, Darius Garland, Kyrie Irving, Onyeka Okongwu and Zach Edey, then Jaden McDaniels, Dylan Harper, CJ McCollum, Jeremiah Fears, Nikola Topic (said as "Namay Ka"), Jusuf Nurkic and Quentin Grimes. He knowingly built a risky, injury-prone core. His reason is that the market overreacts to the risk around Davis and Irving. He comments on value and reach picks throughout, plus situations like Derik Queen likely losing the New Orleans starting job to Yves Missi, Jalen Duren's unresolved situation and Khaman Maluach likely starting in Phoenix. His main takeaways: mock drafts help but every draft goes differently, 10-team rosters are much more stacked, and late in shallow leagues you should be aggressive and chase upside because the waiver wire is full. The final projected standings were very tight, and his team finished second in the projections.

rules.text: Mock drafts have some use, but every draft is very different. Don't fixate on mock trends, or you will be thrown off when your real draft goes differently.
rules.quote: we have to make sure we're not narrow focusing and thinking that that is the only way that a draft can run

rules.text: In a 10-team league teams are much more stacked than in a 12-team league, so players fall further than usual.
rules.quote: It is a 10-man league so teams are going to be a little bit more stacked

rules.text: The gap between 10-team and 12-team leagues is big. Some teams get a player like LeBron James with their sixth pick.
rules.quote: The difference in a 10 and 12 man league, it is it is pretty stark, honestly in terms of just how stacked

rules.text: In a 10-team league, be more aggressive with upside picks late. The waiver wire is full all season, so failed picks are easy to replace.
rules.quote: this a 10-man league be more aggressive. Your in a in a 10-man league, your waiverwire is brimming.

rules.text: Late picks with no upside, like a low-ceiling backup, are pointless when better-value options are available.
rules.quote: There's just so many other options who are better value at that spot.

rules.text: Once you are in flyer territory late in the draft, just take your upside flyers. Don't try to game ADP to wait on them.
rules.quote: it is flyer territory so just take my flyers.

rules.text: Check your team's category strengths and weaknesses during the draft and pick to fill needs, such as adding a big man for rebounds or reaching for assists.
rules.quote: My rebounds need to be improved. So, I probably do need a big man coming up soon.

rules.text: Sometimes you have to reach to fill a category need, like taking a player a bit early just to get assists.
rules.quote: I think I am desperate for assists. I'm just going to take Dylan Harper. I don't love it.

rules.text: Pairing several injury-risk players is risky. He thinks the market is overindexing on risk for some veterans, which creates value.
rules.quote: It's risky to have this combination of players, but I think we're also a little bit overindexing on the risk

rules.text: Panicking when your targets get sniped leads to bad picks. Have a clear backup in your queue.
rules.quote: that's a mistake for me cuz I panicked and which can happen in drafts.

rules.text: Check positional eligibility as the draft goes so your roster positions are covered, leaving only flex spots at the end.
rules.quote: Got to make sure that my positions look okay. I've just got I need a small forward.

rules.text: A late pick can serve as insurance on a star by taking a teammate who should start.
rules.quote: I'm just going to take Grimes just as a sort of Luca somewhat insurance.

rules.text: Role players with upside like McDaniels gain value when a teammate misses time, because they get a usage spike.
rules.quote: If somebody misses time, he just gets a usage spike.
